The call ends with a specific day and time set, but two structural loose ends â€” unclear appointment logistics (drone shot / bill required before locking the schedule) and end-of-call confusion about who visits the home â€” leave the booking more fragile than the smooth middle of the call suggests.
outcome_dispute: The appointment has a specific day (tomorrow) and time (9:30 AM) stated aloud, which meets the bar for 'booked' on datetime_captured. However the rep explicitly conditions the schedule slot on receiving the roof photo and utility bill first ('I would need the picture of the roof and then the utility bill before I can put you in the schedule'), so this is better read as tentative/conditional rather than a clean booked outcome.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: conditional appointment gating without lead-type context
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I mean, I would need the the picture of the roof and then the utility bill before I can put you in the schedule.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The appointment as booked is contingent on two customer deliverables not yet in hand, which materially affects whether this sit will hold — the manager should confirm this customer's lead type and coach the rep on whether this gate was necessary or an avoidable fragility.

key_moments.quote: and I was just wondering what the cost would be to put on solar panels.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer asks a pricing question directly out of the gate. The rep never explicitly answers or redirects this with the schema's price-deferral language; he simply moves on to house lookup. This isn't a rep failure per se — deferring detailed pricing to the closer is correct setter-scope procedure — but the question was never acknowledged or bridged, leaving it open for the closer to walk into cold.

key_moments.quote: I'd say about a $120 a month.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep captures the bill figure but the very next thing he does is soften it ('Not, like, the highest bill') rather than flip it into alignment-against-the-utility. This is capture-and-move-on, the schema's named failure pattern, not capture-and-flip.

key_moments.quote: I have five mini splits in the house.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer volunteers a detail indicating a high electric load (five mini-split heat pump units) immediately after giving his bill figure. This is exactly the kind of unsolicited usage signal that should raise the value of the lead in the rep's eyes, but the rep's response treats it as a neutral acknowledgment rather than a hook.

key_moments.quote: in Virginia, the main requirement to get solar right now is having a credit score above 6 50. Is that the case for you?
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep states 650 as the credit threshold. The schema's documented threshold is 670, and this is a second corroborating instance of the same drift already flagged in SESSION18_fcbf33c1 (Meg), where the rep also said 650. This is a schema_drift_detection finding, not a coaching failure on this individual rep — it suggests 650 may be common floor language, or the schema's 670 is stale.
